A1.justification: The authors, method equations, and matching experiments establish the same work despite retitling. Both PDFs are readable, but v2 ends after its references and lacks v1's Appendices A–G despite retaining appendix references. Main-text comparison is reliable; supplementary continuity cannot be verified. Omissions below refer to the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original TAS classification results, component ablations, architecture comparisons, and supplementary experiments on CIFAR100 and ImageNet-1K.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification results and ablations under the renamed FBT method in Tables 1–6.

M1.justification: TAS becomes FBT, but the documented procedure remains the same: shared CNN and MSA/MLP modules connected through L2G, pooled final features, OFA and InfoNCE losses, and three teacher/fusion/student supervision terms. The adaptive-fusion framing does not establish a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR100 and ImageNet-1K image classification. Object detection and NLP remain proposed future applications rather than evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator sets. However, v1's additional FCFD comparison on three heterogeneous CIFAR100 pairs (Appendix B, Table 8) is absent from v2; FCFD remains in the homogeneous comparison. The added TS taxonomy entry and newly cited methods are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained main experiments preserve their stated datasets, resizing, accuracy metric, optimizers, and training budgets. v1's separate KD-only progressive and multiteacher evaluation design (Appendix D, Table 9) is absent from v2. This contracts the documented evaluation procedures without establishing changes or reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: The main ablations remain, but v2 omits substantial targeted supporting analyses: progressive distillation (Table 9), FitNet feature-stage/pooling/loss comparisons (Table 10), alternative L2G attention blocks (Table 11), computational cost (Table 12), and channelwise feature visualizations (Figure 6). These omissions reduce evidence addressing why the design works.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averages across model pairs are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main student accuracies in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. Table 2 changes the ResNet50 teacher accuracy for Swin-N from 82.05 to 80.38. For CIFAR100 Swin-T→ResNet18, Table 4 changes the no-InfoNCE result from 79.28 to 80.95, reducing its deficit from 2.33 to 0.66 points; the unchanged 79.26 direct-supervision ablation has its deficit corrected from 0.66 to 2.35. The substantial change is the additional absence of v1's supplementary results in Tables 8–12 and Figure 6.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit mathematical claim that OFA loss equals KD loss when gamma=1 and temperature=1. The displayed loss formulas and architectural composition otherwise remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introductory Figure 2 narrows the novelty claim from the first generic feature-based distillation method for arbitrary pairs to one of the pioneer works. The core claims of generic heterogeneous distillation and the headline accuracy gains remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 narrows MSE's stated unsuitability from any teacher–student pair to some pairs. v2 also explicitly attributes homogeneous-distillation benefits to aligning different modules, while dropping v1's developed multiteacher-complementarity discussion. The principal limitations concerning homogeneous-teacher advantages, spatial alignment, and untested domains remain.

D1.justification: v2 announces an available code repository instead of a future release. However, it omits Appendix A/Table 7's detailed training recipe, including batch sizes, learning rates, schedules, augmentation, and loss hyperparameters, plus Appendix F's implementation explanations and Table 12's resource figures. These are substantial disclosure changes, not demonstrated changes to the underlying settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Liu et al.'s Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation and Wu et al.'s heterogeneous contrastive distillation, explaining their exclusion from experiments through reported reproduction difficulties. It narrows the novelty positioning and omits Appendix B's extended FCFD discussion and several references, while retaining the main related-work framework.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, TAS/assistant terminology becomes FBT/fusion throughout, and the introduction and method motivation are substantially rewritten around adaptive knowledge fusion. Loss supervision becomes Section 3.3, ablation headings are reorganized, acknowledgments are added, and the appendix sections are absent.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is rearranged and moved onto the opening page; Figure 2 adds a TS comparison panel; v1's CNN/MSA/MLP explanatory Figure 3 disappears. Remaining diagrams are relabeled and repositioned, table captions and layouts change, and appendix Tables 7–12 and Figure 6 are absent.

improvement.justification: As supplied, v2 substantially weakens reproducibility and supporting evidence by omitting the detailed training recipe and targeted pooling/loss, projector, progressive-distillation, and cost analyses, while still directing readers to unavailable appendices. Numerical corrections, more qualified novelty positioning, and a stated code link are useful improvements, but do not compensate for this loss of checkable support. The core method and main benchmark results remain largely unchanged.
